plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, lavishly ruffled blooms open in clouds of pink, blush and white, often with a sweet, rose-like perfume. Each flower can reach the size of a salad plate and bends its stem after rain.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, typically May to early June in temperate northern gardens
plants.location: Temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens, including the northern United States, Europe and northern China
plants.funFact: Peonies are famously long-lived, and a single plant can keep flowering in the same garden for more than 50 years. Ants are often seen on the buds, where they feed on sugary nectar.

plants.name: Rosa banksiae
plants.description: A vigorous, thornless climbing rose that smothers walls, fences and trees in cascades of small, delicate, softly scented flowers. When it blooms, entire facades turn into waterfalls of pale yellow or white.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, with peak bloom from late April into May
plants.location: Native to central and western China; widely grown in the southern United States and Mediterranean climates
plants.funFact: A Lady Banks' rose planted in Tombstone, Arizona, in the 1880s is often cited as the largest rose bush in the world, with a trunk that has spread over a vast arbor.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful tree that drapes itself in trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. When the blossoms drop, they carpet streets and lawns in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, roughly May to June; in the Southern Hemisphere, October to November
plants.location: Native to South America; grown in subtropical regions including Mexico, southern California and Florida
plants.funFact: In some places, a jacaranda flower landing on your head is said to bring good luck. In Pretoria, South Africa, the trees are so abundant that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.
